newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares set high,seen losing steam Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares set high,seen losing steam Wednesday.

text.p: Polish shares set their third straight 30-month high on Tuesday but analysts said the lower turnover signalled a relatively flat market on Wednesday as many investors would likely take profits.
But they said if firms' August earnings results, the bulk of which are due after Wednesday's session, proved good, the market could keep rising.
"Good company earnings could provide the next impulse," said Adam Drozdowski, an analyst at BGZ brokerage.
Analysts said August's industrial production figure, due later on Tuesday, could help forecast how earnings will be.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 1.3 percent to 14,809.5 points and turnover fell 14.9 percent to 158.7 million zlotys ($57 million) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 31 to 23 with 23 stocks flat.
Analysts said that a downward correction over the next few sessions would likely not take the bourse below 14,300 points.
They said a good sign was that several large-cap stocks such, as banks, were rising, signalling institutional buying.
Banks WBK, Bank Gdanski, BRE and BIG all rose between 4.3 percent and 5.3 percent.
Analysts also said recent gains were linked to rises on major Western bourses.
They said top gainer construction firm Espebepe, up 9.7 percent, was likely helped by Monday's news it had sold a subsidiary and its debt for 2.9 million zlotys ($1 million).
Continuous trade turnover was at 1.7 million zlotys ($0.6 million) with biggest mover trader Universal up 1.8 percent.
Mass privatisation NFI units, which rose 2.5 percent to 121 zlotys ($43.5) in the regular bourse session, rose 1.6 percent to 123 zlotys ($44.2) in 5.4-million-zloty ($1.9 million) continuous trade.
